Human trafficking is a grave crime defined by international law as the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, or receipt of persons through force, fraud, or deception for the purpose of exploitation. This exploitation encompasses forced labor, sexual slavery, servitude, or organ removal. The United Nations Palermo Protocol—formally the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children—establishes the globally recognized legal framework. It explicitly states that trafficking involves exploitation that "shall include, at a minimum, the exploitation of the prostitution of others or other forms of sexual exploitation, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, servitude, or the removal of organs." Crucially, the law emphasizes that consent of the victim is irrelevant; even if someone initially agrees to a job, if they are subsequently coerced, deceived, or trapped through threats, debt bondage, or abuse of vulnerability, it constitutes trafficking.
